function: p. 1-3: Channel estimation: a GNN maps received pilot signals, plus user locations, to the cascaded user-IRS-BS channels of an IRS-aided uplink system.
system: p. 2-3: Uplink multiuser MISO, BS with M=16 antennas, K=4 single-antenna users, passive reflecting IRS with N=80 elements; carrier frequency/band not stated.
method: p. 3-4: Graph neural network with FNN aggregation and combination layers (S=2), trained offline and supervised by an MSE loss against true cascaded channels; Adam.
data_channel: p. 3-4: Custom simulator: Rayleigh direct channel, Rician IRS channels (β=30 dB), cited path-loss formulas; 10000 training and 1000 test samples; no standard or measured data.
test_conditions: p. 3, 5: Same simulated setup (M=16, K=4, N=80) for training and testing; trained at Pu=10 dBm, tested at other powers (Fig. 6); also imperfect user locations, β=20 dB.
baselines: p. 3: Non-learned LMMSE [11]; learned FNN and CNN applied to the same estimation problem; GNN without user locations (ablation) and with imperfect locations.
metrics: p. 3-5: Normalized MSE (NMSE) of the estimated cascaded channels versus pilot overhead and uplink transmit power; training-epoch convergence (Fig. 4).
complexity: p. 5: FLOPs order of GNN, FNN, and CNN given as closed-form O(.) expressions; the GNN is stated to be less complex than the FNN; no runtime.
q1_support: p. 3: "The direct channel hd,k is assumed to follow Rayleigh fading" and "We assume the Rician fading model"; custom simulator, with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data mentioned.
q2_support: p. 5: "we test the trained GNN under different uplink transmit power", an SNR sweep; no other scenario, array size, band, or dataset is tested, and the text does not say whether the beta=20 dB case was retrained.
q3_support: p. 3: "other DL schemes such as FNN and CNN" and "the non-DL approach, i.e., LMMSE [11]"; p. 5: "outperforms other channel estimation schemes under low pilot overhead" (NMSE).
q4_support: p. 5: "The required FLOPs of the S aggregation and combination layers in (8)" and the order O(.) of the GNN, FNN, and CNN are given as formulas.
q5_support: p. 4: "we generate 10000 samples and 1000 samples to train and test the neural networks"; data come from the authors' own simulator, and no code or data link or public dataset is given.
notes: Included, area 2: the learned function is channel estimation of an IRS-aided link; user locations are an input feature, so this is not localization. Frequency band is never stated. The FNN and CNN baselines are the authors' own implementations of standard architectures (Tables I and II, p. 4), counted as learned baselines. Path-loss formulas are cited from refs [10], [11], not stated to come from 3GPP. q2 stays 0 because Fig. 6 (p. 4) only sweeps the transmit power of a model trained at 10 dBm, and Fig. 5 shows a beta=20 dB curve without saying whether the model was retrained; the reviewer may want to check this point.
